description_full: Shionogi & Co., Ltd. engages in the research, development, manufacture, and distribution of pharmaceuticals, diagnostic reagents, and medical devices in Japan and internationally. It is also involved in consumer healthcare business; manufacturing, sale, analytical testing, and pharmaceutical engineering of medicinal drugs and investigational drugs; contracted monitoring of epidemiological components in sewage; promotion of implementation in social infrastructure; and business related to providing data and information; develops and sells foothold; and research and development of mucosal vaccines. In addition, the company provides contract support services for experimental research; contract testing of agricultural production materials; solutions for education and healthcare, system development, human resource development, and training business; marketing support services; and IT services for medical and healthcare-related issues. The company was formerly known as Shionogi Shoten Co., Ltd. and changed its name to Shionogi & Co., Ltd. in 1943. The company was founded in 1878 and is headquartered in Kita, Japan.

financial_summary: Shionogi & Co. Ltd. is a large-cap healthcare business with a $16.5B market cap on $3.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 18% against a 8% cost of capital — a 10-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 85% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $1.1B in free cash flow — roughly 36 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.04× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 19× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.1% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 4.4% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 3.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

news_headlines.title: Shionogi & Co., Ltd. (SGIOF) Set to Post Earnings on Thursday

sect: Its 33% operating margin runs 34pp above the Healthcare median (0%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 3.81x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.05 across 462 companies in the universe; the top four hold 35% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 5% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 25% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 65% and a beta of 0.63, it is more defensive than the market.
Trading is thin (about $4K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 38% in the 2020 crash and 38% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 30% below its DCF fair value of $27.55, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 20%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $22.81 to $35.10 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Healthcare peers: P/E 10.8 vs 26.2, EV/EBITDA 1.8 vs 15.5 and P/FCF 14.5 vs 23.8 (sector median).
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 6.9% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 0.3% (vs the 8% bar).
The price implies 5.5% annual cash-flow growth, 7pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 18% clears the cost of capital of 8.0% by 10pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have been steady (CV 0.18).
It runs a 85% gross margin and converts 36% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 1.04x, but a weak Piotroski score of 3/9.
ROE of 12% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.5x equity multiplier).
SG&A jumped 26% last year, worth watching.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $2.1B.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.2, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 1.7% over 3 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
own: Insiders own a modest 4.4%, and institutions hold 60%.
It returns 2.1% a year to shareholders (0.0% in buybacks and 2.5% in dividends).
people: With about 6,223 employees, each generates about $503K of revenue, 1.3x the Healthcare median.
That works out to $183K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.9M (4x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (1/10, lower is better).
